clue.text: Reasonable tune queen's mate used in playing violin

indicators.note: one set of letters is used inside another, so the tune and mate go into the playing

parts.note: playing a violin is fiddling
an air is a tune
a queen is a female cat, and her mate is a tom

explanation.surface: A tune fit for a queen's consort is performed on the violin and judged reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty, but in crosswords it is often a female cat, whose mate is a male cat. 'used in' puts the tune and mate inside the playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair to middling is an idiom for moderately good, neither bad nor excellent, so it means reasonable.

clue.text: Straightening leg Tin Man bust

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so these letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: The Tin Man from Oz has a broken leg that needs straightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as broken in the surface and is the anagram signal for LEG TIN MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Alignment is the act of putting things into a straight line, a noun matching straightening.

clue.text: Romeo with every single one making pass

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
each means every single one

explanation.surface: Romeo, with every one of his friends, makes a pass at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a point and to pass it can both mean arrive at or get to, as in reaching a milestone.

clue.text: Firm that's erected circus tent employs well-armed individuals

indicators.note: in a down clue something erected stands upwards, so the firm's letters read bottom to top

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the big top is a circus tent
to employ is to use

explanation.surface: A company that puts up a circus big top hires strongmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns CO into OC, a natural action for a tent firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopuses have eight arms each, so they are jokingly well-armed creatures.

clue.text: Climbers from India struggle on peak in Switzerland

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: the peak of a word is its top, first letter, taken from Switzerland

explanation.surface: Mountaineers from India battle on an Alpine summit in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbers' suggests mountaineers, but it means climbing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivies are climbing plants that scale walls and trees.

clue.text: Stop holding back, saint is most dull

indicators.note: one word holds another, so the back goes inside the stop

parts.note: an engine that dies stops
the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A command to stop holding something back, followed by a remark that a saint is very boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop holding back' reads as one instruction, but Stop is DIE, which holds REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and gloomy, so the superlative is the dullest.

clue.text: Opening of one no-trump men raised

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no-trump

indicators.note: in a down clue raised letters are read upwards, reversing the men

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A bridge player opens bidding one no-trump while men raise the bid.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening section of a piece of music or writing.

clue.text: Turned tad grey at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, someone turned slightly grey with seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyrated means rotated or spun round, so it is a synonym for turned.

clue.text: Be sure to hold appeal for goal

indicators.note: one word holds another, so the appeal sits inside the sure thing

parts.note: 'you bet' means be sure, so bet means be sure
to ask is to appeal

explanation.surface: A footballer is told to hold the ball and appeal for a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: In basketball, a goal is scored by putting the ball through the basket.
explanation.definitionFit: In basketball the basket is both the hoop and a successful shot, the goal.

clue.text: Name of woman a consumer reported

indicators.note: something reported is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a consumer is an eater, so 'an eater'

explanation.surface: A shopper's name is given in a report.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'an eater' sounds like ANITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is a female given name.

clue.text: Margin accepted by one doing trial period

indicators.note: one word accepts another inside it, so the margin goes into the trialist

parts.note: someone who runs a trial is a tester
a rim is an edge or margin

explanation.surface: A margin of error is accepted by someone carrying out a trial period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial period' looks like one phrase, but 'period' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is a period of about three months, as in pregnancy or an academic term.

clue.text: Core of workers in vessel showing affinity

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter, here from workers

parts.note: a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: Key crew members on a boat show a close bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinship is a family relationship or close connection, hence an affinity.

clue.text: Outer garment for medieval person, as court windy

indicators.note: something windy is blown about, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A medieval courtier needs a coat because the court is draughty.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcoat was a loose tunic worn over armour in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Body parts goatee thankfully hides

indicators.note: the words hide the answer within their run of letters, across the gap

explanation.surface: A man is glad his goatee beard covers his bad teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth are parts of the body, in the mouth.

clue.text: Keep money from house party in Bedfordshire town

indicators.note: the party is put in the town's name, after its first letter

parts.note: Luton is a large town in Bedfordshire, an English county north of London
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A house party in an English town keeps money from someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is an English county just north of London; 'in' places the party inside its town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out on someone is an idiom for withholding something, such as money, from them.

clue.text: South American author regularly dreads being shelved

parts.note: US means American
to author is to pen

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from dreads, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A South American writer often dreads having a book shelved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'author' is a verb here: to pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspended plan is put on hold, which is what being shelved means.

clue.text: Band heading hit entertainment venue

indicators.note: in a down clue one word heads another, sitting above it

parts.note: a strip is a band, as of cloth
to club is to hit

explanation.surface: A band's lead single is a hit at a music venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip club is a nightclub where strippers perform, a kind of entertainment venue.

clue.text: European characters announced grand ladies

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: Dutch esses: S letters, characters that are European because they are Dutch

explanation.surface: Titles of European noble ladies are proclaimed at court.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchesses are noblewomen of the highest rank below royalty, grand ladies.

clue.text: What might make you stir alive if slack?

definitions.text: What might make you stir alive if slack?

indicators.note: slack means loose, so these letters are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what could rouse you when you are feeling lethargic.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and 'slack' also loosens the letters of STIR ALIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vitaliser is something that invigorates, rousing a sluggish person back into energy.

clue.text: Token elevated cleric keeps where in French church?

indicators.note: one word keeps others inside it
in a down clue elevated letters read upwards, reversing the cleric

parts.note: REV, short for Reverend, is a cleric
the French for where is ou

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman asks where a token is kept in a French church.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher is a token exchangeable for goods or services.

clue.text: Returned skirt of silk with tailored pleats

indicators.note: the whole thing is sent back the other way
the skirt of a word is its edge, its outer letters, from silk

parts.note: tailored cloth is cut

explanation.surface: A silk skirt sent back to the tailor for its pleats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' reverses SK plus CUT, SKCUT, to TUCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucks are folds stitched into fabric, like pleats.

clue.text: Son bitter about A levels

indicators.note: about means turned round, so bitter is read backwards

parts.note: tart means sour or bitter

explanation.surface: A son resents his A-level exam results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A levels' are British school-leaving exams; here 'A' and 'levels' do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, as of rock or society, which are levels.

clue.text: Hirsute Parisian's one with small hooter

parts.note: un is French for one
a horn is a hooter

explanation.surface: A hairy Frenchman with a little nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' is British slang for nose, but here it is a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Unshorn means not shaved or cut, so hairy, which is what hirsute means.

clue.text: Hollow squash on smooth woody plant

indicators.note: a hollow word keeps only its shell, the outer letters of squash

parts.note: to rub can mean to smooth

explanation.surface: A hollow squash is placed on a smooth woody stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree with several stems.

clue.text: Specialised hospital, charming nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the charming word holds the hospital

parts.note: nice means charming or pleasant

explanation.surface: A specialist hospital has charming nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' reads as a noun but is a verb holding H.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche market or product is a specialised one serving a narrow group.

clue.text: Man of science tears up novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A scientist rips up a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist and microbiologist behind pasteurisation.

clue.text: Ride moving up South Beach

indicators.note: in a down clue moving up shifts a letter higher, to the top

parts.note: a horse is something to ride

explanation.surface: A ride along a beach heading north to the south shore.
explanation.definitionFit: The shore is the land at the edge of the sea, a beach.

clue.text: That woman's call to back a liberal dissident

parts.note: that woman is her

indicators.note: going back means read backwards, the call reversed

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness

explanation.surface: A woman calls for support for a liberal rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretical means holding unorthodox views against established doctrine, like a dissident.

clue.text: Place where you find actors start

definitions.meaning: actors at work are ..., read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Onset is the beginning of something, as in the onset of winter, a synonym for start.

clue.text: Bird trio breeds with barn shaking

indicators.note: shaking things up mixes them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Three birds breed in a barn that is shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin redbreast is the full name of the European robin, a small bird.
